boundary_rationale: This row opens a fresh koh-amar-YHWH oracle within the continuing Babylon judgment complex: oshb:Jer.51.1 (byte tier) opens כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, echoed in the verse’s own words, “I will raise up against Babylon...a destroying wind” (web:Jer.51.1). The formula is the narrator’s own direct report rather than a formula quoted through a human mouth, so it carries full frame-ownership weight here. The commissioned archers and the Chaldean slain continue the same decree to its grounds clause, oshb:Jer.51.5 (byte tier) כִּ֠י לֹֽא אַלְמָ֨ן יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל, “Israel is not forsaken, nor Judah, by his God” (web:Jer.51.5), before a fresh discourse-imperative frame opens the material that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the flight command and the foreign lament that follow into this same row would keep the whole destroying-wind sequence in one long unit, but their own discourse-imperative and voice shifts mark a further tier-1 seam.

device_notes: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.50.46 (setumah, single-witness) immediately before this row’s own koh-amar onset, corroborating the row-internal seam without implying a parent-level break, since the nations_oracle parent continues from its own onset. This chapter carries four koh-amar-YHWH onsets in all (sweep: 4 verses), each a narratorial reintroduction of the divine voice rather than a formula quoted through a human mouth, so the false-prophet quotation hazard attested in Hananiah’s own speech elsewhere in the book does not bear on this span.

boundary_rationale: A fresh discourse-imperative onset opens this row: oshb:Jer.51.6 (byte tier) נֻ֣סוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֗ל, “Flee out of the middle of Babylon! Everyone save his own life!” (web:Jer.51.6), shifting from the archers’ commission to a direct address urging escape. The golden-cup metaphor and the embedded foreign voice, “We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed” (web:Jer.51.9), carry the same imperative-opened unit through the returning exiles’ own words before the Median mobilization command opens fresh material.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the embedded foreign voice into its own row is defensible given its shift to a first-person foreign speaker, but it carries neither a fresh koh-amar nor a word-event formula of its own, so folding it under the shared flight command reads more conservatively.

boundary_rationale: This row is bounded by a genre shift rather than a formula onset: oshb:Jer.51.15 (byte tier) עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ, “He has established the world by his wisdom” (web:Jer.51.15), turns from second-person judgment address to a third-person hymn about the Creator, the doxology twin of oshb:Jer.10.12-Jer.10.16 (cross-reference as texture, not read as a boundary driver by itself). boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar onset carrying the full divine title stack opens this row: oshb:Jer.51.33 (byte tier) כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, echoed in “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor” (web:Jer.51.33) — the stacked title YHWH of Armies, the God of Israel is a recurring Jer signature (32 verses book-wide). strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the harvest-metaphor oracle forward into the extended response that follows would track one argument running from judgment-decree to Zion's answer, but the fresh koh-amar onset with the full divine title bounds this row more narrowly.

boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar onset answers the preceding lament: oshb:Jer.51.36 (byte tier) לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, “Therefore Yahweh says:” opening “I will dry up her sea, and make her fountain dry” (web:Jer.51.36). boundary_rationale: A discourse-imperative vocative opens this row: oshb:Jer.51.45 (byte tier) צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י, “My people, go away from the middle of her” (web:Jer.51.45), addressing the covenant people directly rather than describing Babylon in the third person. The row-internal therefore-behold-the-days-come formula at oshb:Jer.51.47 (byte tier) לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים recurs almost verbatim at oshb:Jer.51.52 (cross-reference as texture). boundary_rationale: This row opens at a header-internal date frame rather than an oracular formula: oshb:Jer.51.59 (byte tier) הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא, “The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah” (web:Jer.51.59), dated by בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ, “in the fourth year of his reign” — the year-word here is grammatically distinct from the sleep-noun homograph used twice earlier in the chapter, though the two nouns share a construct spelling. The command to write and read the scroll, its performance (“bind a stone to it, and cast it into the middle of the Euphrates”, web:Jer.51.63), and its spoken interpretation are held as one symbolic-act unit, since no tier-1 seam intervenes between command, performance, and interpretation. The row, and the part, end exactly at the byte-asserted colophon: oshb:Jer.51.64 (byte tier) עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ, “Thus far are the words of Jeremiah” (web:Jer.51.64), closing ch 51 before the appendix that follows and marked by its own setumah.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the date-bearing commission from the reading-and-sinking performance would separate the command from its own performance and interpretation, but the one-unit treatment of a symbolic act's command, performance, and interpretation keeps them together without an intervening tier-1 seam.
